mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 7.5%, it signals a weak labor market that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods when UNRATE > 7.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5% and the monthly change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 0.2%, it signals an inflationary risk that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS<0.5 and CPIAUCSL monthly change>0.2%) (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth > 2% and unemployment rate < 5%), a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.5% signals the end of the cycle and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods when the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1>2% and UNRATE<5%) is active and FEDFUNDS>1.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction (HOUST) above 900 thousand units signals strong housing market demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when HOUST > 900 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) falls below 95, it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods when INDPRO < 95 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the employment level (PAYEMS) declines by more than 0.5% monthly and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 7.5%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods meeting the trigger condition (PAYEMS monthly change < -0.5% and UNRATE>7.5) (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong demand regime (defined by GDP growth > 2% and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) above 400,000 million dollars), a rising HOUST index above 900 thousand units signals continued economic strength and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when the strong demand regime (GDPC1>2% and RSAFS>400,000) is active and HOUST>900 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
